title: FloodGuard Private Flood Policy — When Coverage Begins
content:
Underwriting guide section for the FloodGuard Private Flood Policy on waiting periods, the effective date and the attachment of midterm limit increases.

## 1. The waiting period and the effective date

1.1 Coverage starts after a waiting period counted in calendar days from the application date, which is the bound date. The effective date is the bound date plus the waiting days.

1.2 The waiting days are the tier's own figures: its standard waiting period, its loan-closing waiting period, its map revision waiting period and its midterm-increase waiting period, as the tier's waiting period schedule states them.

1.3 A voluntary purchase waits the tier's standard waiting period.

1.4 A purchase required by a lender in making, increasing, extending or renewing a loan waits the tier's loan-closing waiting period, but only when the application and premium are received no later than the loan closing date; otherwise it waits the standard waiting period. This is judged on the purchase reason and the bound date on the policy record together with the loan closing date the named insured states.

1.5 A renewal paid within the renewal grace period, and a transfer of the policy to a buyer of the building, carry no waiting period.

1.6 A bound policy moves to in force on its effective date.

1.7 A flood that begins before the effective date is never covered, even when the water reaches the building after it.

## 2. Map revision purchases

2.1 The map revision waiting period applies only when the policy is applied for within the map revision window that starts on the map revision date.

2.2 The map revision window is counted in calendar months from the map revision date, falling back to the last day of the month when that day does not exist, and an application on the same day of the last month of the window is outside it.

2.3 A map revision purchase waits the tier's map revision waiting period, and only when the revision placed the building in zone A, AE or VE; after the window it waits the standard waiting period.

2.4 The window is judged on the map revision date and the purchase reason on the policy record for the same customer and property address, before the policy is bound.

**Boundary cases (hypothetical dates, a window of 13 months, the figure on every FloodGuard tier).**

| Map revision date | Last day inside the window | First day outside the window |
|---|---|---|
| 15 March 2024 | 14 April 2025 | 15 April 2025 (same day of the last month) |
| 31 January 2024 | 27 February 2025 | 28 February 2025 (31 February does not exist; the last day of the month is used) |

An application on 14 April 2025 after a 15 March 2024 revision into zone AE takes the map revision waiting period; an application on 15 April 2025 waits the standard waiting period.

## 3. Midterm limit increases

3.1 A midterm limit increase waits the tier's midterm-increase waiting period from the request date, or the loan-closing waiting period when the increase is tied to a loan, and the new limit attaches on the date the waiting period ends.

**Worked example (hypothetical).** On a tier with a 14-day midterm-increase waiting period, a voluntary building limit increase requested on 3 May attaches on 17 May. The same increase, tied to a loan on a tier whose loan-closing waiting period is 0 days, attaches on 3 May.
